mainTopic: Why the משנה says אלמנה, רב פפא's challenge from רבי יוחנן's מצרי rule (answered with תנא ושייר), and רב's ruling that fit women may marry disqualified men
overview: This amud covers three topics. First, the גמרא explains why the משנה's first case speaks of an אלמנה: the word is borrowed from the סיפא, where a כהן גדול marrying an אלמנה makes her a חללה, so she is forbidden even to a כהן הדיוט brother. Next, רב פפא challenges the משנה. רבי יוחנן ruled that the son of a מצרי שני and a מצרית ראשונה is a מצרי שני, and that rule produces a new set of cases that the משנה should have listed. The גמרא answers תנא ושייר: the משנה did not list every case. After a long back-and-forth, it proves this by showing that פצוע דכא was also left out. Finally, the גמרא turns to רב's ruling that women fit for כהונה were not warned against marrying disqualified men. A suggested proof from the משנה's word 'fit' is rejected. רבא answers רבין בר נחמן's objection from 'they shall not take': a woman is forbidden only where the man is forbidden. The amud ends by explaining why the כהונה prohibitions need their own source to include women.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that the first marriage decides her status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers a possible defense for why the משנה said אלמנה. The idea is that this תנא judges her by her status at the first marriage. The גמרא rejects it, because the משנה's case of a חלל shows we do not follow that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say that this תנא holds that her status at the first marriage is what counts when she falls to יבום, that cannot be. Look at the case of a חלל who married a woman who was כשרה. There we clearly do not say the first marriage decides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible answer to its earlier question about why the משנה said אלמנה, and then knocks that answer down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested defense: if the first marriage decides, then a woman who married as a בתולה would still count as a בתולה for a כהן גדול. That is why the משנה would need to say אלמנה. But in the חלל case, the woman was כשרה when she married. She only became a חללה through that marriage, and the משנה still forbids her to the brother. So the משנה clearly does not judge her by her status at the first marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say — introduces a possible answer the גמרא is about to reject
The first marriage determines her status when she falls to יבום
A son of a כהן born from a forbidden union, who lacks כהונה status
A woman fit to marry a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not give the גמרא's real answer. It only rules out one possible answer. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you would say
that this tanna holds
that the first marriage is what determines her status when she falls to yibum
but look, a ḥalal who married a woman fit for a priest
and there we do not say that the first marriage determines her status!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off a possible defense to the question (asked just before this section) of why the משנה said אלמנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that this תנא follows נישואין הראשונים מפילין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's own חלל case forbids a woman who was כשרה at her first marriage, so the משנה cannot hold that the first marriage decides.

steps.title: Widow was chosen because of the later clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה said אלמנה in the first case only because of the סיפא. In the סיפא, a כהן גדול married an אלמנה, and that detail really matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word 'אלמנה' is surely there because of the סיפא. The תנא wanted to teach there: a כהן גדול who married an אלמנה and has a brother who is a כהן גדול or a כהן הדיוט. There it must be an אלמנה. If she were a בתולה, she would be fit for the כהן הדיוט brother. Because of that, the תנא says אלמנה in the רישא too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer: the first case said אלמנה just to match the wording of the later case, where אלמנה actually makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a כהן גדול marries an אלמנה, he makes her a חללה, so she becomes forbidden even to a כהן הדיוט brother. If he had married a בתולה, he would not make her a חללה, and she could do יבום with the כהן הדיוט. So the word אלמנה is needed in the סיפא, and the רישא copies it to keep the wording parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה
The High Priest
An ordinary priest
Specifically; only in this exact case
She is fit for him

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה said אלמנה in the first case only to match the סיפא. There, a כהן גדול marrying an אלמנה makes her a חללה, so she is forbidden even to a כהן הדיוט brother.

phrases.english: That is certainly because of the latter clause,
because he wants to teach in the latter clause:
A High Priest who married a widow,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ אָח כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל אוֹ כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: and he has a brother who is a High Priest or an ordinary priest.
Specifically a widow is forbidden to the ordinary priest brother,
phrases.notes: Marrying her made her a חללה, which forbids her even to an ordinary כהן.

phrases.english: but a virgin would be fit for him,
therefore he teaches 'widow' in the first clause too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the suggested defense, the גמרא gives its own explanation for the word אלמנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word אלמנה in the רישא seemed unnecessary, since even a בתולה would be forbidden to a כהן גדול by the time of יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written to match the סיפא, where אלמנה is truly needed for the כהן הדיוט brother.

steps.title: רב פפא's challenge built on רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא raises a challenge. רבי יוחנן ruled that the son of a מצרי שני and a מצרית ראשונה counts as a מצרי שני. If that is right, the משנה should have taught one more case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: if the report is true that רב דימי brought, when רבי יוחנן said that a מצרי שני who married a מצרית ראשונה has a son who is a מצרי שני, then the משנה should also teach this case:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts a new challenge. This line is setting up the case he will describe in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An Egyptian convert and his son may not marry a born Jew. The third generation may (דברים 23:9). רבי יוחנן's rule means the child's generation follows the mother. That opens the door to a new case of מותרות לבעליהן ואסורות ליבמיהן, which רב פפא says the משנה should have listed.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; raises a strong challenge
If it is so; if that statement is true
A second-generation Egyptian convert, still forbidden to marry a born Jew
A first-generation Egyptian woman convert
Let him also teach

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
If that statement is true,
that when Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael,
he reported that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A second-generation Egyptian who married a first-generation Egyptian woman,
her son is a second-generation Egyptian,
then let the mishna also teach:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the משנה's list of cases, separate from the אלמנה discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of cases of מותרות לבעליהן ואסורות ליבמיהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוחנן's rule is true, there is another such case. The משנה should have included it.

steps.title: The Egyptian case the משנה should have taught
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא describes his case. A מצרי שני married a מצרית ראשונה and a מצרית שנייה and had a son from each. If each son married a wife who is permitted to him, each wife is forbidden to the other brother for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצרי שני married two Egyptian women, one first-generation and one second-generation, and had sons from each. If the sons married in their proper way, the wives are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their יבמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his challenge by laying out the exact case he thinks the משנה is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son of the first-generation mother is a מצרי שני, so he marries a second-generation Egyptian woman. The son of the second-generation mother is third-generation, like a regular Jew, so he marries a regular Jewish woman. If one brother dies, his wife cannot do יבום with the other. The Jewish woman is forbidden to the מצרי שני, and the מצרית שנייה is forbidden to the third-generation brother.

keyTerms.meaning: A second-generation Egyptian woman
They married in their proper way, each to a woman permitted to him
Permitted to their husbands
Forbidden to their brothers-in-law for יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Even though both sons have the same father, they are different generations. Under רבי יוחנן's rule, each son's generation follows his own mother.

phrases.english: A second-generation Egyptian who married two Egyptian women,
one first-generation and one second-generation,
and he had sons from the first and from the second.
If they married in their proper way,
phrases.notes: The second-generation son marries a second-generation Egyptian woman; the third-generation son marries a regular Jewish woman.

phrases.english: they are permitted to their husbands
and forbidden to their yevamin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's challenge by spelling out the case introduced in the previous step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This case fits the משנה's pattern exactly, so its absence suggests the משנה does not accept רבי יוחנן's rule.

steps.title: The Egyptian case gives all four outcomes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא shows that his מצרי case can produce every outcome the משנה lists. So the משנה should have taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they switched and married the other way, the wives are permitted to their brothers-in-law and forbidden to their husbands. If they married converts, the wives are permitted to both brothers. If they married barren women, the wives are forbidden to both brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes building his challenge. He shows that the two Egyptian brothers fit every pattern the משנה teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 he showed one pattern: each wife is permitted to her husband and forbidden to his brother. Now he adds the reverse pattern, a 'permitted to both' case (converts) and a 'forbidden to both' case (an אילונית). Since the משנה lists cases like these but leaves this one out, it seems the משנה does not agree with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reversed; the other way around
Brothers-in-law who would do יבום
Women who converted
Women who cannot have children; there is no יבום with them

phrases.english: And if they reversed it and married —
phrases.notes: Each son married the woman who would have suited his brother.

phrases.english: they are permitted to their brothers-in-law
and forbidden to their husbands.
Permitted to these and to those — converts.
Forbidden to these and to those — barren women!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case רב פפא began describing in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the son of a מצרי שני and a מצרית ראשונה is a מצרי שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case matches every pattern the משנה teaches, yet the משנה leaves it out. That suggests the משנה does not hold like רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The תנא taught some cases and left some out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה never meant to list every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some cases and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא. The משנה is not a complete list, so missing this case proves nothing against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's challenge assumed the משנה lists every case. This answer removes that assumption, so a missing case is no longer evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught some cases and left others out

phrases.english: He taught and left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: The list is not complete (תנא ושייר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists every possible case, so a missing case means the משנה disagrees
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left this case out on purpose, along with others

steps.title: What else was left out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for another case the משנה left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we should say he left this one out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer from step 6. It is setting up the next move by asking for a second missing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that 'he taught and left out' only works if more than one case was left out. So the גמרא needs another example to back up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He left out

phrases.english: What did he leave out, that he left out this?
phrases.notes: He means: name another missing case, so this one isn't the only thing missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Another case the משנה left out

steps.title: He left out פצוע דכא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names פצוע דכא as the other missing case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out the case of a man with crushed testicles (פצוע דכא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second missing case. A פצוע דכא can create the same kind of 'forbidden to one brother, permitted to the other' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a second missing case, the answer 'he taught and left out' now holds up. That keeps רבי יוחנן's ruling safe for now.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose reproductive organs are injured, so he may not marry a Jewish woman

phrases.english: He left out a man with crushed testicles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פצוע דכא is another case the משנה left out

steps.title: פצוע דכא is already covered by חייבי לאוין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that פצוע דכא is not really missing, because the משנה taught the general rule of חייבי לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of פצוע דכא, that is not something left out, because he already taught the rule of those forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 8. פצוע דכא is a לאו case, and the משנה already gave the general rule for all לאו cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the general rule covers פצוע דכא, then the משנה did teach it, just not by name. So we are back to having only one missing case, the מצרי case.

keyTerms.meaning: Something left out
Marriages forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)

phrases.english: If it is because of a man with crushed testicles —
it is not something left out,
since he taught those liable for a prohibition!
phrases.notes: The משנה gave a general rule about all marriages forbidden by a לאו, and פצוע דכא is one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that פצוע דכא was left out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case covered by a general rule in the משנה has not really been left out.

steps.title: The משנה lists לאו cases anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה often spells out specific לאו cases even after the general rule. So leaving out פצוע דכא is a real omission.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that he does not teach the general rule of לאוין and then teach specific cases again? But he does teach a regular כהן who married an אלמנה, and a חלל who married a woman fit for a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer of step 8. The משנה does list specific לאו cases by name, so it should have listed פצוע דכא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples are לאו cases already covered by the general rule, yet the משנה spells them out. So the general rule does not stop the משנה from listing cases, and פצוע דכא really was left out. That gives two missing cases, and 'he taught and left out' stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A woman fit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Is that to say that those liable for a prohibition
he does not teach and then teach again?
phrases.notes: He means: teach the general rule, and then also list specific cases.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁנָּשָׂא אַלְמָנָה,
phrases.english: But he teaches a common priest who married a widow,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 2, where his brother is a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and a חלל who married a fit woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין מִי לָא קָתָנֵי וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and supports step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows from the משנה's own style that it lists specific cases even after a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the general rule of לאוין covers פצוע דכא, it was not left out
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists specific לאו cases too, so leaving out פצוע דכא is a real omission

steps.title: The specific case was needed to teach רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 10. The specific case the משנה spelled out was not a plain repeat. It was needed to teach the ruling of רב יהודה in the name of רב that fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case was needed to teach us what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the example from Step 10 does not prove that the משנה repeats cases for no reason. That case was there to teach a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 claimed the משנה spells out specific לאוין even after the general rule, so leaving out פצוע דכא would be a real omission. The reply is that this case teaches something extra: a woman fit for כהונה is allowed to marry a disqualified man. So the proof that the משנה repeats cases for no reason falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
They were not warned (not forbidden)
Fit women, such as women fit to marry a כהן
Disqualified men, such as a חלל

steps.confusionAlert: The direction can be tricky here. The גמרא is now arguing that the specific cases each teach something new. If that is true, the משנה never repeats for no reason, and leaving out פצוע דכא would no longer look like a real gap.

phrases.english: That one, it was needed to teach us
phrases.notes: "That one" means the specific case from the משנה that the גמרא brought up in the last step.

phrases.english: like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
For רב יהודה said that רב said:
Fit women were not warned
against marrying disqualified men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 10's answer by showing the repeated case has its own new law.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the משנה spells out specific cases after the general rule without adding anything.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cited case is not a plain repeat. It teaches רב's ruling.

steps.title: More specific cases in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 11 by pointing to two other cases the משנה spells out: a חלל who married a fit woman, and an Israelite with a ממזר brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: a חלל who married a fit woman, and an Israelite who married an Israelite woman and has a brother who is a ממזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to more cases in the משנה that seem to repeat the general rule. This suggests the משנה does spell out cases even after the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if one case is explained by רב's ruling, these two cases look like plain examples of the general rule. If they add nothing, the משנה does repeat cases, and the omission of פצוע דכא is real again.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches
A man born from a marriage forbidden to a כהן, who loses כהונה status
A child born from a forbidden relationship such as incest or adultery

phrases.english: But it teaches:
A חלל who married a fit woman,
and an Israelite who married an Israelite woman
and he has a brother who is a ממזר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 11 by pointing to other spelled-out cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה never spells out cases without a new reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These two cases seem to be plain examples of the general rule, so the משנה does repeat cases.

steps.title: Each case teaches a different kind of prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that these two cases are not plain repeats either. One shows a prohibition that does not apply to everyone, and the other shows a prohibition that applies to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is not just teaching the same thing again. It taught us a prohibition that is not the same for everyone, and it teaches us a prohibition that is the same for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that each of the two cases adds something. Together they show that the rule works for both kinds of prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלל case is a prohibition that applies only to כהנים, so it is not the same for everyone. The ממזר case is a prohibition that applies to all of ישראל. Since each shows a different type, neither one is a plain repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Going back and teaching again
A prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone
A prohibition that applies equally to everyone

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי, לָא מִהְדָּר מִיתְנָא הִיא,
phrases.english: This too is not just teaching again,
for it taught us a prohibition that is not the same for everyone,
phrases.notes: This is the חלל case, since the rules of כהונה apply only to כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מַשְׁמַע לַן לָאו הַשָּׁוֶה בַּכֹּל.
phrases.english: and it teaches us a prohibition that is the same for everyone.
phrases.notes: This is the ממזר case, which applies to all of ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי, לָא מִהְדָּר מִיתְנָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by giving each case its own purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case teaches a different category, so neither is a repeat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two cases seem to be plain extra examples of the general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: One shows a prohibition that is not the same for everyone and the other shows one that is, so each adds something.

steps.title: A case that really is a repeat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the case of an Israelite who married a ממזרת. This is another prohibition that applies to everyone, so it adds nothing new beyond the ממזר case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: an Israelite who married a ממזרת and has a brother who is an Israelite (and a ממזר who married a ממזרת and has an Israelite brother).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a case that cannot be explained as teaching a new type of prohibition. It is a second example of a prohibition that applies to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 already used the ממזר case to show a prohibition that applies to everyone. The ממזרת case is the same type, so it really is a repeat. This shows the משנה does spell out cases that add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: A female ממזר
A brother who is a regular Israelite of fit lineage

phrases.english: But it teaches:
An Israelite who married a ממזרת
and he has a brother who is an Israelite
(and a ממזר who married a ממזרת
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets here.

phrases.english: and he has an Israelite brother),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 13 with a case that cannot be explained as a new type.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every specific case in the משנה teaches something new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ממזרת case is a second example of a prohibition that applies to everyone, so it is a plain repeat.

steps.title: Conclusion: the משנה taught some cases and left others out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה taught some cases and left others out (תנא ושייר), and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this that the תנא taught some cases and left others out. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section: since the משנה does spell out cases that add nothing new, leaving out פצוע דכא is a real second omission. So 'he taught and left out' stands, and the missing מצרי case is no proof against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה spells out cases even when they add nothing, the general rule does not explain why פצוע דכא is missing. The only explanation left is that the תנא simply did not list every case. This confirms the answer from Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so
Learn from this
He taught and left some out; the list is not complete

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list is not complete. It taught some cases and left others out (תנא ושייר), with פצוע דכא as a second real omission. So the absence of the מצרי case does not disprove רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
he taught and left some out.
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from the challenge in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה taught some cases and left others out. פצוע דכא is a real second omission, so the missing מצרי case does not prove the משנה disagrees with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Back to רב's ruling about fit women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to look at the ruling of רב יהודה in the name of רב on its own: fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב יהודה said that רב said: fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by bringing back the ruling of רב that was quoted in passing in Step 11. It is setting up a discussion of this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling means that a woman fit to marry a כהן is allowed to marry a disqualified man, such as a חלל, even though this marriage makes her unfit for כהונה afterward. Now the גמרא will look for a source that supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; returning to a statement quoted earlier in passing

phrases.english: The matter itself.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to רב's ruling from Step 11 to look at it properly.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
Fit women were not warned
against marrying disqualified men.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about the ruling quoted in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women fit for כהונה are allowed to marry men who are disqualified.

steps.title: A suggested proof from the חלל case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's case of a חלל who married a fit woman supports רב. It reads "fit" as a כהנת fit for כהונה, and the משנה allows the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: "A חלל who married a fit woman." Is it not talking about a כהנת who is fitting for him? And what does "fit" mean? Fit for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a possible proof for רב from the משנה. The question is phrased to set up a reading of the word "fit."
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "fit" means a woman fit for כהונה, then the משנה is describing such a woman married to a חלל, and it allows the marriage. That would support רב, who says fit women may marry disqualified men.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him
Is it not so that
A daughter of a כהן
Fit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
"A חלל who married a fit woman,"
is it not talking about a כהנת [who is fitting for him],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and what does "fit" mean?
Fit for כהונה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for support in the משנה for the ruling stated in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that fit women may marry disqualified men.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of a חלל who married a fit woman, read as a woman fit for כהונה.

steps.title: Maybe 'fit' means a regular Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב: the משנה's 'fit woman' may just be a ישראלית who is fit to marry into the Jewish people, not a כהנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about an Israelite woman. And what does 'fit' mean? Fit to marry into the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the last step. It says the 'fit woman' in the משנה might not be a כהנת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 read 'fit' as 'fit for כהונה,' meaning a כהנת, so the משנה would show that a כהנת may marry a חלל. Here the גמרא offers another reading: 'fit' means fit for the קהל, an ordinary Jewish woman. If so, the משנה says nothing about a כהנת, and the proof for רב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish woman who is not from a כהן's family
Fit to marry into the Jewish people
The congregation, meaning the Jewish people as a whole

phrases.english: No, it means an Israelite woman.
And what does "fit" mean?
Fit to enter the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17 by reading the word 'fit' differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה for רב's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Fit' does not have to mean a כהנת; it can mean a ישראלית fit for the קהל.

steps.title: The 'fit brother' shows 'fit' means fit for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If 'fit' means fit for the קהל, then 'a fit brother' would suggest the dead חלל was unfit for the קהל, which is wrong. So 'fit' must mean a כהן, and then the woman must be a כהנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'he has a fit brother' would also mean fit for the congregation. That would imply that he, the חלל, is unfit for the congregation! Rather, doesn't it mean a כהן? And since he is a כהן, she must be a כהנת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 18 and tries to bring back the proof for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה also says the חלל has a 'fit' brother. If 'fit' means fit for the קהל, it would suggest that the חלל himself was not fit for the קהל. But a חלל is only unfit for כהונה, so that reading cannot be right. 'Fit' must mean fit for כהונה, and to be consistent, the 'fit woman' must be a כהנת.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a problem that follows from the last idea
By implication; it follows that
Not allowed to marry into the Jewish people
Rather, isn't it...? Introduces the reading the גמרא wants to prove

phrases.english: If so:

phrases.aramaic: ״יֵשׁ לוֹ אָח כָּשֵׁר״, נָמֵי כָּשֵׁר לַקָּהָל,
phrases.english: "He has a fit brother" would also mean fit for the congregation,
which implies that he is unfit for the congregation!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the חלל who died. That can't be right, since a חלל is only unfit for כהונה, not for marrying a regular Jew.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean a priest?
And since he is a priest, she must be a priest's daughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 18 and brings back the proof from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'fit' means fit for the קהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'fit' is used for the brother. Read that way, it would wrongly suggest that a חלל is unfit for the קהל. So 'fit' must mean fit for כהונה in both places.

steps.title: Each 'fit' can be read in its own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two uses of 'fit' do not have to match. The brother is fit for כהונה, and the woman is fit for the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge from step 19. The word 'fit' does not have to mean the same thing for the brother and for the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the brother, 'fit' means fit for כהונה, the opposite of his חלל brother. For the woman, 'fit' means fit for the קהל. Since each case is read on its own terms, the משנה still does not prove that a כהנת may marry a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that comparable? Used to reject linking two cases
This one as it is, and that one as it is; each case has its own meaning

phrases.english: Is that comparable?
This one is as it is,
phrases.notes: The brother's 'fit' means fit for כהונה.

phrases.english: and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: The woman's 'fit' means fit for the קהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא — הָא כִּדְאִיתָא וְהָא כִּדְאִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19, so the proof from the משנה stays rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The argument that both uses of 'fit' must mean the same thing
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing forces the two uses of 'fit' to match; each fits its own case.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove רב's ruling, because the 'fit woman' could be an ordinary ישראלית.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the woman is warned through the man
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר נחמן objects to רב from a ברייתא. The repeated phrase 'they shall not take' teaches that the woman is warned through the man, which seems to mean a כהנת may not marry a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר נחמן objected: 'They shall not take ... they shall not take.' This teaches that the woman is warned through the man!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב comes from a ברייתא that reads a פסוק about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men. The ברייתא learns from the double 'they shall not take' that a woman is also warned through the man's prohibition. That seems to say a כהנת is warned against a חלל, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall not take; a prohibition on כהנים marrying certain women
Is warned; is under a prohibition
Through the man; by means of his prohibition

phrases.english: Ravin bar Nachman raised an objection:
"They shall not take ... they shall not take,"
this teaches that the woman is warned
through the man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, a new challenge against רב comes from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the woman is warned through the man, which seems to forbid a כהנת from marrying a חלל.

steps.title: The woman is warned only where the man is warned
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא only means the prohibition works from both sides. Where the man is forbidden, the woman is forbidden. Where he is not forbidden, she is not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Wherever he is warned, she is warned. And wherever he is not warned, she is not warned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבין בר נחמן's challenge and protects רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not create a separate prohibition for women. It only says that when a man is forbidden to a woman, she is forbidden to him too. A חלל is not forbidden to marry a כהנת, so she is not forbidden to marry him, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Wherever; in every case where
(He) is warned; under a prohibition

phrases.english: Rava said:
Wherever he is warned,
she is warned;
and wherever he is not warned,
she is not warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּהוּא מוּזְהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 21 by limiting what the ברייתא teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to warn women on their own, so a כהנת would be forbidden to a חלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman's prohibition only follows the man's prohibition. Since a חלל is not forbidden to a כהנת, she is not forbidden to him.
steps.whatToRemember: In these marriage prohibitions, the woman's prohibition mirrors the man's. If he is not forbidden, neither is she. This is why a כהנת may marry a חלל, as רב said.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions. A כהן may not marry a חללה, but a כהנת may marry a חלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב's ruling that fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.

steps.title: Why is a special source needed for the woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's source. We already know from 'a man or woman' that women and men are equal for all Torah punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn this from here? We learn it from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: 'A man or woman who commits any of the sins of people.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all punishments in the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא from step 21. Why do we need the repeated 'they shall not take' to teach that the woman is warned, when another פסוק already teaches it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the doubled phrase 'they shall not take' to show that the woman is included in the prohibition. But רב יהודה, quoting רב and the school of רבי ישמעאל, already has a general rule: women are equal to men for every punishment in the Torah. So the doubled phrase looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from here
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
The פסוק made them equal
Punishments

phrases.english: But is this learned from here?
phrases.notes: 'This' means the ברייתא's lesson that the woman is warned just like the man.

phrases.english: It is learned from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav!
As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught the same:
'A man or a woman who commits'
any of the sins of people'
The verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the punishments in the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא? מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נָפְקָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the argument about רב to a question about the ברייתא's own source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of the doubled 'they shall not take' to include the woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק already makes women equal to men for all punishments, so the special source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The general rule covers only prohibitions that apply to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The general source would only cover prohibitions that apply to all people. The כהונה prohibitions apply only to כהנים, so the ברייתא needs its own source.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we learned only from that פסוק, I would have said it covers a prohibition that applies to everyone. But a prohibition that does not apply to everyone, it would not cover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the ברייתא needs its special source. The general rule might not reach prohibitions that apply only to some people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A man or a woman' makes women equal to men in prohibitions that apply to all Jews. The marriage limits of כהונה apply only to כהנים, so we might think women are left out of them. The doubled 'they shall not take' teaches that even these prohibitions include the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
A prohibition that applies equally to everyone
A prohibition that does not apply to everyone (like the כהונה rules)

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule that women equal men for punishments covers prohibitions that apply to everyone. A prohibition limited to one group, like כהנים, needs its own source to include women.

phrases.english: If we learned only from that one, I would have said:
a prohibition that applies equally to everyone, yes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לָאו שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל, לָא.
phrases.english: But a prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by limiting how far the general source reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the competing source, so the ברייתא's source is still needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women would be equal to men only in prohibitions that apply to all Jews, not in the כהונה rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled 'they shall not take' is needed to include women in the כהונה marriage prohibitions.
